prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M; grid, port out of scope. Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment; availability reviewed); Main Transformer (site-specific trip); export cable→Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; applies Dispatcher ceiling). Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss; shutdown on confirmed fire), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor (degradation data), Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss; no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Degraded (fault/comms/environment/external limit, no full shutdown), Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby, Turbine Lockout (no remote restart during fire investigation). Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard; fleet status). Alarms: safety>protection>export; not cleared on detector reset. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; operational records→Shore Control Room; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway). Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; hub; holds last limit on grid comms loss). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; completion review). Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft). Personnel Tracking Console (route entry/exit). Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Duty Planner adjusts priorities from reliability findings. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. HSE Officer: evacuation advice. Field Supervisor: work status→Shore Control Room; procedure feedback. Control Engineer records deviation findings. Warehouse System: failure data→spares review. Cybersecurity Analyst reviews cyber impact on availability. Corrective actions need owner, due date, verification. North Access Scanner: credential/period/area; gate secured if unverifiable; no verbal override; unique transaction ID. Southern scanner: timestamped logs; barrier closed on failure; anti-tailgating; escorts verified;

New part:
S935: The system records the affected function, the detected condition, and the time of transition so that operators can assess the scope and duration of the impairment.
S936: Safety functions take priority over energy production, maintenance throughput, and schedule recovery in every degraded mode.
S937: Turbine Controller retains protective control locally when the supervisory connection is unavailable, while the Shore Control Room monitors the loss of visibility.
S938: If remote commands cannot be confirmed, the Control Engineer suspends those commands and uses approved local procedures until reliable control is restored.
S939: The Weather Service and Weather Analyst support entry into Weather Hold when forecast or observed conditions exceed approved operating limits.
S940: A turbine with a safety-critical fault is placed in Turbine Lockout until the fault is assessed and the required work is authorized.
S941: The Offshore Substation enters Substation Degraded when a protection, auxiliary supply, or monitoring impairment limits safe switching or export capability.
S942: The Grid Interface Relay applies the configured response to a Grid Constraint, and the Grid Dispatcher is advised when generation capability changes.
S943: Marine activity is reduced or suspended in Vessel Standby when weather, visibility, communications, or vessel capability is insufficient for safe transfer.
S944: The Marine Coordinator and Vessel Master confirm that personnel and vessels can remain safely accounted for during an extended interruption.
S945: The Fire Detection Panel and Emergency Generator remain essential services during degraded operation and are not bypassed to recover production.
S946: The SCADA Gateway preserves available status and alarm information, while the SCADA Engineer investigates missing or inconsistent indications.
S947: The Fleet Dispatch Console presents operational restrictions so that the Duty Planner can prioritize urgent safety work and maintainable generation capacity.
S948: The Maintenance Planning Engine separates safety-critical work from tasks that can safely wait until normal access and support are available.
S949: The HSE Officer reviews any proposed workaround that changes established access, isolation, or personnel-control arrangements.
S950: A degraded condition is escalated when its duration, uncertainty, or effect on adjacent equipment increases beyond the approved operating envelope.
S951: The Control Engineer coordinates technical recovery with the relevant field and shore roles before any protection or operating restriction is removed.
S952: Recovery begins only after the initiating condition has been corrected or bounded and the responsible operator has confirmed that the equipment is stable.
S953: Required inspections and functional checks are completed before affected equipment is returned to automatic control or normal duty.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
